structuredContent.guidelines:
# roam/agent guidelines <roam uid="XcDxM3AGm" refs="10"/>

- This is the **discourse-graphs team graph** (dg-team). It tracks product development, user research, and design knowledge for the Discourse Graphs project. Start orientation at [[🚪 Discourse graphs front page for team members]]. <roam uid="ZyEFQdPzy"/>
- Graph Ontology <roam uid="CkMv_I9Hu" heading="2"/>
  - This graph uses a discourse graph node grammar with typed nodes. Each node type has a title format that the Roam plugin uses for identification via regex. Nodes exist at two levels of formality: <roam uid="JZ-ERybz9"/>
    - **Full node pages** — titled with the type prefix (e.g., `[[ISS]] - description`). These are the primary knowledge units. <roam uid="Lr2QOC061"/>
    - **Candidate nodes** — blocks tagged with a candidate hashtag (e.g., `#iss-candidate`, `#res-candidate`). These are seedling ideas not yet promoted to full pages. <roam uid="IxTd36BlH"/>
  - Node Types: Knowledge <roam uid="iJARoph1H" heading="3"/>
    - **Question (QUE)** — the unknowns being explored through pilots and research. Format: `[[QUE]] - {content}`. Sections: Summary, Notes, Testable hypotheses, Snippets. <roam uid="9uXF_YcQQ"/>
    - **Hypothesis (HYP)** — proposed answers to questions; collect evidence for or against. Format: `[[HYP]] - {content}`. Candidate tag: `#hyp-candidate`. Sections: Rationale, Snippets, Requests for Experiments. <roam uid="jA0VLkwMY"/>
    - **Result (RES)** — a discrete observation from ongoing research, in past tense. Format: `[[RES]] - {content} - {Source}`. Candidate tag: `#res-candidate`. Sections: Summary, Grounding Context, Snippets. Properties: NodeFormality (Draft → ReadyForInternal → ReadyToShare → Published), Contributors. <roam uid="21s0GTu6p"/>
    - **Evidence (EVD)** — a discrete observation from a published dataset or experiment. Format: `[[EVD]] - {content} - {Source}`. Sections: Evidence Description, Snippets, Grounding Context, Centrality slider. <roam uid="zgYL5nVb4"/>
    - **Claim (CLM)** — an assertion about how discourse graphs work or should work. Format: `[[CLM]] - {content}`. Candidate tag: `#clm-candidate`. <roam uid="9SOQK_533"/>
    - **Source (SRC)** — a referenced publication or external resource. Format: `@{content}`. <roam uid="wenbahwqN"/>
    - **Theory (THE)** — a theoretical framework or model. Format: `[[THE]] - {content}`. <roam uid="UtoPH2BxJ"/>
  - Node Types: Product & UX <roam uid="e-gV24nNQ" heading="3"/>
    - **Function (FUN)** — a UX "use case": a specific situation where Discourse Graphs can be used to enhance the experience. Tool-agnostic in framing, but tied to a concrete user goal. Format: `[[FUN]] - {content}`. Properties: FunctionImportance, FunctionScoping. <roam uid="LjYlqRpUR"/>
    - **Flow (FLO)** — a set of interactions the user performs to accomplish a goal within a particular implementation of Discourse Graphs (Obsidian plugin, Roam plugin, tldraw, etc.). A Flow is the tool-specific instantiation of a Function/Use Case. Format: `[[FLO]] - {content}`. Sections: Description (Goal, Loom, brief description), Steps (Normal flow, Alt flows, Exceptions), Examples, Pain points. Properties: FlowStatus (💭 Hypothetical → 🗓️ Planned → 🤔 Experimental → 🚧 Bespoke → 🔨 Alpha → 🚀 Beta), FlowFrequency, FlowImpact. <roam uid="SVcbz9E3i"/>
    - **Artifact (ART)** — the features, workflows, and UI components we build to enable Flows and Use Cases (Functions). Parts of a system are prefixed with the system name (e.g., `[[ART]] - Roam DG/Query`). Format: `[[ART]] - {content}`. Properties: ArtifactType (Feature/Component or Workflow/Template), ArtStatus (🤔 Prospective → 🖇️ Bespoke → 🧪 Alpha → 🎯 Beta → 💎 Release → 🌐 External). <roam uid="71FJwPgwi"/>
    - **PainPoint (PAI)** — problems, friction, and bottlenecks in user experience. Format: `[[PAI]] - {content}`. Properties: Activity, Function, Flow, UserTool. <roam uid="zD3lBBh9A"/>
    - **Journey (JOU)** — a user journey across multiple functions/flows. Format: `[[JOU]] - {content}`. Sections: Description, Phases, Pain points, Notes. <roam uid="YmhUG6VJX"/>
    - **Activity (ACT)** — an action the user performs that is not specific to any particular tool or method (e.g., "synthesize literature," "discuss findings"). Activities sit upstream of tool-bound Flows and Use Cases. Format: `[[ACT]] - {content}`. <roam uid="1NcVa1g2X"/>
    - **UserPilot** — a specific user or pilot engagement. Format: `UserPilot/{content}`. Properties: User status, UserTool (Roam, Obsidian, Notion, tldraw), UserType (Alpha/Beta/Normie), Lead. <roam uid="5XUZyDshG"/>
    - **CaseStudy (CAS)** — a documented case study. Format: `[[CAS]] - {content}`. <roam uid="ceCyzY2Ei"/>
  - Node Types: Project Management <roam uid="L4Lo_4B1w" heading="3"/>
    - **Issue (ISS)** — a potential action item for development or research. Format: `[[ISS]] - {content}`. Candidate tag: `#iss-candidate`. Properties: Issue Status (🤔 Considering → 🗓️ Backlog → 🗓️ Planned → 🚀 Active → 💬 Awaiting Feedback → ➡ Sent To Linear → ✅ Complete → 🧊 Iced → ⏸️ On hold), Issue Type (🗳️ Feature Request, 📄 Template improvement, 🐞 Bug Report, 🔬 Research, 🏗️ DG team, 🛠️ Maintenance), Priority, Project, Function, Flow, Lead. <roam uid="jzczOjTM1"/>
    - **Project** — a research or development project. Format: `Project/{content}`. Properties: Project Status (🗓️ Backlog → 🗓️ Planned → 🚀 Active → ✅ Complete → 🧊 Iced → ⏸️ On hold), Priority. <roam uid="IwUFa4By7"/>
    - **Milestone** — a time-boxed delivery target. Format: `Milestone/{content}`. Properties: Milestone Status, Start/End Date, Priority. <roam uid="NCfJPwcoO"/>
  - Relation Types <roam uid="PZxB_Lim1" heading="3"/>
    - **Supports / Supported By** — Evidence or Result supports a Claim, Hypothesis, or Conclusion <roam uid="QLrw6Cikm"/>
    - **Opposes / Opposed By** — Evidence or Result contradicts a Claim, Hypothesis, or Conclusion <roam uid="RdGHvBjvu"/>
    - **Informs / Informed By** — Evidence, Result, or Claim informs a Question or Hypothesis; Question informs Hypothesis; Hypothesis informs Issue <roam uid="0TFxQSHzV"/>
    - **Reproduces / Reproduced By** — Evidence confirms other Evidence <roam uid="lZNpV65LF"/>
    - **Resolves / Is resolved by** — Result resolves an Issue <roam uid="BKCUPTVYB"/>
    - To query typed relations programmatically, use `mcp__discourse__get_relationships uid=…` (the `discourse` MCP) — it returns a node's Supports / Opposes / Informs / Reproduces / Resolves edges and their complements directly. See **Which MCP tool for which task** under Navigating. The `roam` MCP can't resolve typed relations; with it, fall back to following page references within node content and checking linked references. <roam uid="4uQA80UCZ"/>
- Navigating the Graph <roam uid="I5GtkN5Cn" heading="2"/>
  - Which MCP tool for which task <roam uid="0w3wW5Rny" heading="3"/>
    - Two MCP servers read this graph. Reach for the **`discourse`** server whenever a task depends on the discourse-node / relation grammar (typed nodes, typed relations, the ontology); use the **`roam`** server for general text search, reading arbitrary pages, and all writes. <roam uid="v7YWcac84"/>
    - **Find discourse nodes by topic** → `mcp__discourse__search_nodes` (all query words must appear in the node title; optional `node_type_format` regex restricts to one type, e.g. `\[\[FLO\]\]` for Flows). For free-text across __all__ blocks — meeting notes, daily notes, non-node content — use `mcp__roam__search` instead. <roam uid="OmYGreM1F"/>
    - **List every node of a type** (all Flows, all Issues, …) → `mcp__discourse__get_all_discourse_nodes` (optional `since` ISO date for "what's new"). More reliable than a roam prefix search, which can miss nodes. <roam uid="OMwgWxWHS"/>
    - **Read a node's full content** → `mcp__discourse__get_node uid=…` for the title + full block tree; `mcp__roam__get_page` / `mcp__roam__get_block` are the general-purpose equivalents. <roam uid="2LarSnz-g"/>
    - **Find a node's typed relations** (what Supports / Opposes / Informs / Reproduces / Resolves it) → `mcp__discourse__get_relationships uid=…`. Resolves the typed edges directly; the roam server cannot. <roam uid="GS3OMHszL"/>
    - **Walk a node's neighborhood** (multi-hop reference graph) → `mcp__discourse__get_node_neighborhood uid=… depth=1–4 direction=both`. <roam uid="ur9V-QLL7"/>
    - **Get the live ontology** (node types + relation definitions) → `mcp__discourse__get_discourse_node_types`. The source of truth behind the **Graph Ontology** section above — pull it when you suspect the documented types or relations have drifted. <roam uid="qVG4hiqaO"/>
    - **General text search, recency, reading arbitrary pages, and all writes** → the **`roam`** server: `mcp__roam__search` (empty query = recently edited / viewed), `get_page`, `get_block`, `get_backlinks`, `create_block`, `update_block`. The `discourse` server is read-only. <roam uid="Tf4JXJyRu"/>
    - **Read the publication behind an `@source`** → check its `metadata::` / `Abstract::` block first; for full text use the `zotero` MCP (`mcp__zotero__*`) when it's in the user's Zotero library. <roam uid="wsMfcY8Rf"/>
    - **Find who created a block** → `mcp__roam__datalog_query` on `:create/user`. There is no dedicated block-author tool on either MCP server; this query is the only reliable way to get block-level provenance. Always bind it to a page or a uid — unbounded, it returns every block in the graph. <roam uid="YemilM2pX" refs="1"/>
      - By page: `[:find ?uid ?creator ?editor :in $ ?page-title :where [?p :node/title ?page-title] [?b :block/page ?p] [?b :block/uid ?uid] [?b :create/user ?cu] [?cu :user/display-page ?cp] [?cp :node/title ?creator] [?b :edit/user ?eu] [?eu :user/display-page ?ep] [?ep :node/title ?editor]]` — returns uid + names only. Don't add `?b :block/string ?s` unless you need it: it re-returns the whole page you already read, roughly 7x the tokens. <roam uid="7BKClr9BK" refs="1"/>
      - For a single block, replace the two page clauses with `[?b :block/uid ?uid]` and pass the uid as the input. <roam uid="icLRn-ci0" refs="1"/>
    - **Find who created a page or discourse node** → `mcp__discourse__get_node uid=…` returns `author`, `author_uid`, `created`, `modified`. Page-level only — given a __block__ uid it returns the content with no author, so fall back to the datalog query above. <roam uid="wRmrVnFqO" refs="1"/>
    - **List every identity in the graph** → `mcp__discourse__get_users` — humans, bots, and API tokens with their uids. Resolve a partial name here before making any authorship claim. <roam uid="7IXa9Yq2g" refs="1"/>
    - **See what one person wrote recently** → `mcp__discourse__catch_me_up author="…" days=N`. Needs the exact display name from `get_users`. <roam uid="0gEBMNuKz" refs="1"/>
    - **Find the discourse nodes a person authored** → `mcp__discourse__get_researcher_contributions author="…"`. Node __pages__ only — it returns 0 for identities that write blocks but never create node pages, so a 0 is not evidence that someone wrote nothing. <roam uid="0OshhlAu4" refs="1"/>
    - **Filter an existing query by author** → `mcp__discourse__run_discourse_query query_uid=…` honors the query builder's `created by` / `edited by` conditions. <roam uid="MyIALn-lG" refs="1"/>
    - On every call, pass the graph explicitly (`graph="dg-team"`) — several graphs are configured, and the wrong one silently returns nothing. <roam uid="STWu7JWy_"/>
  - Entry point <roam uid="MHzuk97bt" heading="3"/>
    - Start from [[🚪 Discourse graphs front page for team members]], which orients you to the main dashboards, functions/flows, pilot status, and hypotheses/results. <roam uid="nPt2-iVnj"/>
  - Following page references for context <roam uid="h9NTRhMjK" heading="3"/>
    - Much of a node's meaning lives in its **page references** — the `[[double-bracketed]]` links within its content blocks. These connect nodes to the Functions, Flows, Projects, Sources, and UserPilots that give them context. <roam uid="U28zLlsXL"/>
    - When reading a node, expand or follow its page references to understand **why** it exists and **what** it connects to. For example, a Result node's title includes its Source (e.g., `[[RES]] - users synthesized 3x more claims - [[@pilotStudy2025]]`), and its body may reference the Function or Flow it relates to. <roam uid="BQMJ8e_-z"/>
    - **Linked references** (at the bottom of any page) show every block in the graph that mentions that page. This is the primary way to see how a node is used in context — meeting notes, update logs, other discourse nodes, and daily notes entries. <roam uid="G9z0oYOKm"/>
    - **Block references** work similarly for individual blocks (bullets). If a block has a reference count, it has been cited elsewhere. <roam uid="Dcv_AHP0W"/>
  - Search strategies <roam uid="uDgL2s89Q" heading="3"/>
    - Search for discourse nodes by their type prefix: `[[QUE]] -`, `[[ISS]] -`, `[[FLO]] -`, `[[RES]] -`, etc. <roam uid="z9FqVtbYA"/>
    - Search for candidate nodes by their tag: `#iss-candidate`, `#res-candidate`, `#hyp-candidate`, `#clm-candidate`, `#flow-candidate`, `#up-candidate`, `#pro-candidate`. <roam uid="R6ZQgo7E-"/>
    - Search with empty query to see recently edited and viewed content — useful for understanding current activity. <roam uid="aHXgbk2iE"/>
    - For attributes with constrained values (status fields, priorities, tools, etc.), refer to [[roam/js/attribute-select]] for the canonical set of options. <roam uid="MaJPh5WXZ"/>
  - Understanding overall workflows <roam uid="3Qe0kZwzj" heading="3"/>
    - An observation from a pilot (Result) often triggers an idea for improvement (Issue). Issues are higher priority when they improve an important Flow, which in turn enables a key Function. Once engineering works on an issue, it becomes a feature (Artifact). <roam uid="E-6z55uoF"/>
    - Result → Issue → Flow → Function → Artifact traces the path from observation to shipped feature. <roam uid="gFNP0A0S9"/>
- Writing into the graph <roam uid="a7uWA6zlm" heading="2"/>
  - Leave node creation and tagging to the team by default (see **Agent Behavior → General rules** below). When you are explicitly asked to capture something — a candidate node, a pilot observation, a flow — follow these conventions so each block reads cleanly now **and** is trivial to promote into a formal discourse node later. <roam uid="mebOIP95I"/>
  - Put each concept in its own block <roam uid="F3EVfNmD7" heading="3"/>
    - Write one idea — one claim, observation, pain point, flow, or action — per block. Don't pack several into a single bullet. Be parsimonious with any commentary you consider adding. <roam uid="1LMq1Ui6Y"/>
      - Atomic blocks are individually addressable: each can be block-referenced (`((uid))`), tagged, and promoted to a node on its own. A compound bullet can't. <roam uid="rLZacptHP"/>
    - Use indentation to carry structure: the parent block states the idea; child blocks hold its detail, caveats, steps, and references. <roam uid="VFcltIeP4"/>
      - This mirrors a discourse node, where the title is the idea and the template sections are the children. <roam uid="dv7_tHNg5"/>
  - Make candidate blocks formalizable <roam uid="t62zcsYxS" heading="3"/>
    - When you tag a block with a candidate tag, write the statement so it can become the node's **title almost verbatim** — the eventual node title should be roughly the same words as the block. Keep it atomic and self-contained: understandable without the surrounding meeting / log context. <roam uid="QcHWU8FCu"/>
    - Match the target node's title grammar so promotion is mechanical. The candidate tags in use here are `#iss-candidate`, `#res-candidate`, `#hyp-candidate`, `#clm-candidate`, `#flow-candidate`, `#up-candidate`, `#pro-candidate` — each maps to the node type of the same prefix (see **Graph Ontology** above for every format). Common cases: <roam uid="vNFJ3JbII"/>
      - `#res-candidate` → a discrete, past-tense pilot observation → `[[RES]] - {statement} - {Source}`. Name the `@source` / UserPilot in a child so it can be appended to the title on promotion. <roam uid="Xx5QnpXMw"/>
        - Example: `Pilot users created 3x more claims after the canvas node preview shipped #res-candidate` <roam uid="8RsFzOBwL"/>
      - `#iss-candidate` → an actionable dev or research item → `[[ISS]] - {statement}`. <roam uid="0tM9FtTCr"/>
        - Example: `Group nodes on the canvas by semantic similarity #iss-candidate` <roam uid="b8CJepmiH"/>
      - `#flow-candidate` → a tool-specific interaction flow → `[[FLO]] - {statement}`. <roam uid="alG4QCDR4"/>
        - Example: `Preview / view DG node info while on the tldraw canvas #flow-candidate` <roam uid="skG-2mzeZ"/>
    - If you can't yet phrase an idea atomically, leave it as plain text and don't tag it — a vague stub can't be promoted without a rewrite. <roam uid="znTpKgzZv"/>
  - Put supporting context in child blocks <roam uid="YE6FUcUKB" heading="3"/>
    - Everything that explains, grounds, or qualifies a candidate goes in **child blocks beneath it, never crammed into the statement**.  On promotion these children carry over into the node's template sections. <roam uid="VwHNAB0ij"/>
    - `#res-candidate` → Source + method + a screenshot or Loom → **Grounding Context** and **Snippets**. `#flow-candidate` → **Description** (Goal, Loom), **Steps**, **Pain points**. `#iss-candidate` → why it matters + the Flow / Function it improves → Issue Status / Type / Project / Flow properties. <roam uid="-zzjS0GNH"/>
    - Link related nodes with `[[…]]` inside the children — those page references become the node's discourse connections (Supports / Opposes / Informs / Resolves) once it is formalized. <roam uid="pM5ojIoXO"/>
  - Reuse the existing syntax and formatting conventions <roam uid="MEWdJCUaQ" heading="3"/>
    - For how to __reference__ nodes when writing (Roam alias syntax, `((uid))`), follow **Agent Behavior → Citing and referencing nodes** below — don't paste full URLs inside Roam. <roam uid="iqnB7VJ1X"/>
    - For callouts, colors, and foldable blocks, use the palette documented in **Agent Behavior → Formatting** below. <roam uid="1-PwVXvKX"/>
    - Reference only node titles you have actually found in the graph; never fabricate one. Preserve node title regex formats exactly (`[[RES]] - … - {Source}`, `[[FLO]] - …`, `UserPilot/…`) — a malformed title silently drops the block out of the discourse graph. <roam uid="ldsx0Q1Nj"/>
- Agent Behavior <roam uid="HQkVaTtF9" heading="2"/>
  - Information hierarchy <roam uid="Omx-xxku_" heading="3"/>
    - **Prioritize formalized node pages** (full `[[TYPE]] - title` pages with templates filled in). These represent the team's vetted, structured knowledge. <roam uid="gSd5Imn_Z"/>
    - **Then candidate nodes** (`#type-candidate` tagged blocks). These are preliminary but intentionally captured ideas. <roam uid="KPWTNgy6Z"/>
    - **Then remaining content** (meeting notes, daily notes, log entries, comments). These provide context but are less curated. <roam uid="7FBUcDopw"/>
    - Rank by formality, but check authorship before you cite — only human-written blocks are citable. See **Synthesize human content, not agent content** below. <roam uid="RgZPUYxXj" refs="1"/>
  - Synthesize human content, not agent content <roam uid="IxsMpHOOT" heading="3" refs="1"/>
    - **Your job is synthesis of what the team's people wrote.**  Building on agent-authored content closes a loop where agents cite agents and the graph fills with its own echo. <roam uid="2vCRnvaM-" refs="1"/>
    - **This includes your own prior output.** Never cite, quote, count, or treat as evidence a block that you or another agent wrote, in this graph or any other. <roam uid="r-7VcjnUB" refs="1"/>
  - Provenance: who wrote this block <roam uid="psNqP1Ow4" heading="3" refs="1"/>
    - **Never ascribe a statement to a person without querying the block's creator.** Position in the outline, a nearby name, and a `#[[Name]]` tag are not authorship signals — a person tag usually marks an assignee or a mention, and meeting notes are typed by one scribe on everyone's behalf. Look up `:create/user` before writing "X thinks", "per Joel", or any attributed quote. <roam uid="QowkWQTjg" refs="1"/>
    - **When creator and last editor differ, report both.** "Created by `matt-AI-bot`, last edited by Karola Kirsanow" is the honest form. Don't collapse it to one name. <roam uid="ABeXcABpE" refs="1"/>
    - **Speaker initials in meeting notes are the exception, and you should honor them.** On `Sync /` pages, `JC:`, `MAP:`, `MG:`, `KK:`, `MA:` are the scribe's record of who spoke. Attribute the __position__ to the initials and the __block__ to its creator, and say the initials are your basis. <roam uid="zgFhSiYI6" refs="1"/>
    - **If you can't resolve authorship, say the block is unattributed.** Never assign it to the nearest name on the page. <roam uid="CFgMF_i0-" refs="1"/>
    - **Non-human identities in this graph today:** `matt-AI-bot`, `ai-cybrarian`, `cybrarian-ai`, `Michael Gartner (AI)`, and every identity whose display name begins with `API Token:` or `Local API Token:`. Treat those as machine-written unless you have checked otherwise. Per-bot users are still being sorted out — see [[Convention/Human-AI interaction in Roam]]. <roam uid="78YnS6gEC" refs="1"/>
      - A token is not automatically an agent. `API Token: Raycast matt` and `API Token: send2graph` forward text a human typed. Token-created means __provenance unclear__, not __AI-generated__ — report which one you actually found. <roam uid="VBVOklCV1" refs="1"/>
      - `Discourse Graphs`, `Anonymous`, and `Anonymous_1`–`Anonymous_3` are shared or unresolved accounts. Don't attribute their blocks to any individual. <roam uid="rHnvdFRhH" refs="1"/>
    - **You may read agent content as context, but don't cite it.** Use an agent-written summary or digest to locate the human blocks underneath, then read and cite those. Consider the agent-written content as background context, not citable material. <roam uid="tCRWvyruf" refs="1"/>
    - **When the human record is thin, say so.** If the only coverage of a topic is agent-written, report that the team has not covered it rather than laundering an agent's take into a finding. <roam uid="PDwgHjakx" refs="1"/>
  - Citing and referencing nodes <roam uid="1Q-QuB4hm" heading="3"/>
    - When referencing discourse nodes in your responses, use **Roam alias syntax** so the link is readable but navigable: <roam uid="iZecLmaRZ"/>
      - `[the claim about synthesis]([[[[CLM]] - discourse graphs improve synthesis]])` <roam uid="-XCMrdIIk"/>
      - `[this pilot result]([[[[RES]] - users synthesized 3x more claims - [[@pilotStudy2025]]]]])` <roam uid="47VfBEfiy"/>
      - `[canvas node preview flow]([[[[FLO]] - Preview/view DG node info while on canvas]])` <roam uid="9VQN1PcbM"/>
      - `[the grouping issue]([[[[ISS]] - group nodes on the canvas, eg by semantic similarity]])` <roam uid="huKrbfYiZ"/>
    - For block-level references, use the `((uid))` syntax when you have a specific block UID. <roam uid="P03iIKmxK"/>
    - Always include enough of the node title for the reader to understand the reference without clicking through. <roam uid="6rl43A8ym"/>
  - Citing dates <roam uid="FNMHIgv1c" heading="3"/>
    - The team uses the linked references of daily notes pages as a "table of contents" to monitor the team's work that week. Therefore, be judicious in how many times you reference a daily note with wikilinks. The top-level entry usually includes a reference to today's date, and any clear deadline can be referenced once per entry. Other dates should be labeled like `July 29` rather than with wikilinks. <roam uid="AJ-MJrH7M"/>
  - Reading nodes thoroughly <roam uid="UJfOc9mSn" heading="3"/>
    - When investigating a node, don't stop at the title. Read the template sections (Summary, Description, Rationale, etc.) for substance, and follow page references in the content for context. <roam uid="9mWl4_KbG"/>
    - All the firebase links are public links to images.  Usually, these images are very informative, so for relevant nodes and pages you should open the images and interpret them with your image recognition capabilities <roam uid="EIquKiNkw"/>
    - Check linked references to see where the node has been discussed in meetings, logs, and other nodes. <roam uid="rsCUVEZGn"/>
    - For Results and Evidence, pay attention to the Source in the title and the Grounding Context section for methodological detail. <roam uid="rxcu3DrEs"/>
  - Linking to this graph <roam uid="sTxa7aNev" heading="3"/>
    - If you create a URL in the agentic chat UI (outside of roam), remember that the URL starts with `https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/`. The graph url is discourse-graphs; the graph MCP nickname is dg-team. <roam uid="8VfrwIAkz"/>
  - Formatting <roam uid="DLi8zMdfk" heading="3"/>
    - When writing in Roam, you can make use of colors, color underlines, and comments: <roam uid="UPWoTfgXC"/>
      - [[>]] [[!NOTE]] This is a basic note callout\nNotes are great for highlighting general information you want to draw attention to. <roam uid="GRXCvlZXR"/>
      - [[>]] [[!INFO]] Informational callout with an info icon\nUse these for additional context or background details. <roam uid="q9AGKeYbe"/>
      - [[>]] [[!SUMMARY]] A summary or abstract callout\nPerfect for executive summaries, TLDRs, or condensed overviews. <roam uid="-e0ZjrNmx"/>
      - [[>]] [[!TIP]] Helpful tip — try using callouts for emphasis!\nCombine callouts with **bold**, *italic*, and `code` formatting in both the title and body. <roam uid="QZj72rl96"/>
      - [[>]] [[!SUCCESS]] Operation completed successfully\nAll 47 tests passed. The deployment to staging is live. <roam uid="qnaPlXY2m"/>
      - [[>]] [[!QUESTION]] How do callouts work in Roam?\nThe first line after `[[!TYPE]]` is the title. Add body text on the next line with **Shift+Enter**. <roam uid="HQRN8neWv"/>
      - [[>]] [[!WARNING]] Be careful when editing shared pages\nOther users may be viewing or editing at the same time. <roam uid="tAydkxtXR"/>
      - [[>]] [[!FAILURE]] Build failed due to missing dependencies\nRun `npm install` and check that all peer dependencies are satisfied. <roam uid="gzwZx-squ"/>

      - [[>]] [[!EXAMPLE]] Here's how you format a callout\nUse `[[>]] [[!TYPE]] Title` on the first line. Add body text with Shift+Enter. <roam uid="cLHhp8Dwj"/>

  - General rules <roam uid="0lg_blMOv" heading="3"/>
    - **Don't fabricate graph content.** Only report what actually exists. If coverage is sparse on a topic, say so. <roam uid="tSrgNKRUv"/>
    - **Search before concluding something doesn't exist.** Try multiple search strategies: type prefix, keywords, candidate tags, related node titles. <roam uid="i2TsjJ5AL"/>
    - **Respect node title formats.** The Roam plugin identifies node types from title regex. Malformed titles break the discourse graph structure. <roam uid="RpBlhUpIR"/>
    - **Leave node creation and tagging to graph users** unless explicitly asked to create or modify content. <roam uid="AKkPvzUbn"/>
    - **Check `:create/user` before ascribing provenance.** Never attribute a statement, position, or decision to a person without confirming who created the block. Misattribution is worse than saying you don't know. <roam uid="TdWRewexC" refs="1"/>

# Untitled <roam uid="JzkR8n8Li"/>

- Refuse to store a node or relation whose schema did not resolve #iss-candidate <roam uid="ZUPpRUlDm" heading="1" refs="1"/>
  - I think this can be post-v0 <roam uid="iRifHPMB3"/>
  - related to ((9IOlhocYN))<ref>Instances of a deleted schema stay in the database with no schema #iss-candidate</ref> but distinct <roam uid="_5Sl2dyc7"/>
  - Need / Problem Statement <roam uid="OGUWZww1W"/>
    - What is the problem that you are trying to solve? <roam uid="Wu06VbjVz"/>
      - The problem is: `upsert_concepts` stores a node or relation even when its schema cannot be found. The row is written with `schema_id` NULL, which the database then reads as a node with no type, and the client cannot tell this apart from a success. <roam uid="nibZELQuX"/>
      - Background: a client sends each node or relation to `upsert_concepts` with its schema named by local id or RID (`schema_represented_by_local_id`). For a node, the schema is its node type. For a relation, it is its triple. Clients usually send the schemas in the same call, ahead of the instances that use them. <roam uid="hhu1UwmIB"/>
      - The database resolves references in two different ways: <roam uid="CALynweUL"/>
        - A reference to another concept, such as a relation's source and destination, goes into `reference_content`. If it does not resolve, `reference_content` becomes NULL, the NOT NULL constraint rejects the row, and the call returns `-2` for it. Nothing is stored. <roam uid="76LxV5oUA"/>
        - The schema reference goes into `schema_id`, which accepts NULL. If the schema does not resolve, the row is stored anyway, and the call returns its id as for a success. <roam uid="uF4Qscf4L"/>
      - A relation stored without a schema gets `is_relation = false`, derived from the missing schema, so every reader treats it as a node. A node stored without a schema has no type. <roam uid="GfQtmrkzd"/>
      - A schema fails to resolve when its own upsert fails in the same call, for example on a schema name clash (FqKZiG8xr, ENG-2324, ENG-2325), or when the client never sent it, as with the end types fixed in [ENG-2337 Sync and publish cross-space relations from Roam with the exact group check](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2337/sync-and-publish-cross-space-relations-from-roam-with-the-exact-group). <roam uid="MVcuZU5Sq"/>
      - Clients compensate after the fact, and only partly. Roam's publish withholds the grant from a node or relation whose schema failed in the same call, but the row stays in `my_concepts`. Later publishes treat it as synced and do not send it again, so it is never repaired, and it is granted once its schema succeeds. <roam uid="uLwcPG1Cj"/>
    - Who is affected? What are they trying to do, and what is stopping them? <roam uid="2c4SxjzX8"/>
      - Users of both apps who publish or sync nodes and relations. A schema-less row looks stored to the client, so the user gets no error. Group members who import from that space see a relation as a node, or a node with no type. <roam uid="mQ04ppMYs"/>
      - Developers, who have to handle schema failures in every client and every write path. <roam uid="bp6GvGjA5"/>
    - What request, observation, or other evidence supports this? <roam uid="z2ku-trHv"/>
      - A schema-less Obsidian Source node was found in production on September 25 <roam uid="ACm9p-eWE"/>
        -  ((FqKZiG8xr))<ref>A schema created with the name of a deleted schema is refused by the database #iss-candidate</ref>. <roam uid="TjHHg0-Rk"/>
      - Issue candidate ((9IOlhocYN))<ref>Instances of a deleted schema stay in the database with no schema #iss-candidate</ref> describes how a schema-less relation reads as a node, and the decision to delete schema-less Concepts. <roam uid="rqDNGhVJw"/>
      - The publish case was found in the [ENG-2337 Sync and publish cross-space relations from Roam with the exact group check](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2337/sync-and-publish-cross-space-relations-from-roam-with-the-exact-group) code review on October 4, by reading `publishNodesToGroups` and `upsert_concepts`. Not reproduced. <roam uid="t1i0o7OPI"/>
  - Fit and urgency <roam uid="mNIBjNcbm"/>
    - ^^What accepted user, developer, or project need would this address?^^ <roam uid="VI4ZC-v05"/>
      - Reliable sharing of nodes and relations through the database: a stored concept is either complete or absent. <roam uid="Bb0Czi5Rn"/>
    - Is it relevant to work expected within the next six months? <roam uid="ME6cKJ4_1"/>
      - Yes. The cross-space relation tickets ([ENG-2334 Publish relevant cross-space relations](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2334/publish-relevant-cross-space-relations) to [ENG-2340 Import cross-space relations into Roam](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2340/import-cross-space-relations-into-roam)) add more relations whose triples and end types are sent in the same call. <roam uid="gLEypyPv2"/>
    - Why consider it now? What happens if we delay it? <roam uid="DnAMXi7FX"/>
      - Delaying keeps the current state: schema-less rows can be stored silently, and each client has to detect them after the call. ENG-2337 reduced the most likely cause on Roam's publish path. [ENG-2324 Delete stale schemas so a schema recreated with the same name can sync](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2324/delete-stale-schemas-so-a-schema-recreated-with-the-same-name-can-sync) repairs schema-less nodes in Obsidian's full sync. <roam uid="eOfdIdy9L"/>
      - Recovery from existing schema-less rows is the deletion decided in ((9IOlhocYN))<ref>Instances of a deleted schema stay in the database with no schema #iss-candidate</ref>. <roam uid="1UATA_PxI"/>
  - Possible solutions (choose one or both) <roam uid="-zGTST1XT"/>
    - Separate upserts: send schemas in a first call, then send only the instances whose schema succeeded in a second call. <roam uid="8qa7xBEpY"/>
      - Client-side only, no migration. Each write path must be changed: Roam publish, Roam sync, Obsidian publish and sync. <roam uid="3u2Yrkzkx"/>
      - Costs one more call per write. The two calls are not atomic, which is no worse than today: a failure inside one call already leaves the call's other rows written. <roam uid="lQbYin5pr"/>
    - Refuse a schema-less instance in the database: `_local_concept_to_db_concept` raises when `schema_represented_by_local_id` is given but does not resolve. `upsert_concepts` then returns a negative id for that row, as it does for an unresolved reference. <roam uid="2JlsH2hr0"/>
      - Protects every client and every write path at once. Needs a migration. <roam uid="RWGxt1-F7"/>
      - Clients that ignore negative results, as Obsidian does today ([ENG-2325 Report concepts that the database refuses during Obsidian sync](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2325/report-concepts-that-the-database-refuses-during-obsidian-sync)), then skip the row silently instead of storing it. <roam uid="sOCWUT6_0"/>
    - Both: the database rule guarantees the invariant, and separate upserts let a client report a schema failure without sending the instances at all. <roam uid="xnyi-4Zww"/>
    - Either path changes how the sync recovers. Both sync mechanisms select what to send by last-modified time. This is not new: any failed row has the same effect today, for example a schema name clash. <roam uid="Wtd_6BcYv"/>
      - In Roam, any negative result makes the sync throw. The sync's start time then does not advance, so every later sync retries the same rows and fails the same way until the cause is fixed. Turning a stored schema-less row into a refused row turns a silent bad row into a sync that never completes. <roam uid="7ci-4hASW"/>
      - In Obsidian, negative results are ignored and the sync time advances. A refused row is not sent again until the node is edited, unless a full sync re-sends it (ENG-2324 adds this for schema-less nodes). <roam uid="YOCJtbOmT"/>
      - So this needs a decision on how a refused row is retried, whichever path is chosen. <roam uid="Y0uHTors7"/>
  - Triage <roam uid="zbt8ZFjH0"/>
    - Is the need clear enough to create an engineering ticket? <roam uid="7-adVcUj6"/>
      - Not yet. It needs a choice of path, and a decision on how a sync retries a refused row. <roam uid="fii05Bcng"/>
    - Outcome: (proposed) Park <roam uid="zlBT3b8Gl"/>
    - Reason: The database damage is easily reversible. <roam uid="Eylh8wIku"/>
- Instances of a deleted schema stay in the database with no schema #iss-candidate <roam uid="9IOlhocYN" heading="1" refs="5"/>
  - My call: Real but can wait until after v0 <roam uid="WSTBL8j3Z" refs="1"/>
    - For the record, there are 516 Concept rows which are not schemas but also have no schema, probably through this mechanism <roam uid="5JtNKu5zX"/>
  - Need / Problem Statement <roam uid="yZVOgN5Cg"/>
    - What is the problem that you are trying to solve? <roam uid="wHEBNitWv"/>
      - The problem is: when a schema row is deleted, the nodes and relations that point to it stay in the database with an empty schema reference. Nothing can tell what type they are, and relations among them are misread as nodes. <roam uid="OE9YDcsgs"/>
      - A schema is the database row for a node type or a relation type. Each node or relation instance points to its schema through `schema_id`, and the foreign key is `ON DELETE SET NULL`. <roam uid="aqBDM6G6Z"/>
        - Note: This was originally intentional. I thought we could keep the stale information around for examination. I now see it requires complex maintenance. <roam uid="8ql6SW2si"/>
      - This entails a misreading of schema-less relations as nodes. It comes from the `is_relation` column. A trigger (`concept_set_derived_columns`) sets it on every write, from the schema's `roles`, or from the instance's own `literal_content.roles` when it has no schema. Relation instances from Obsidian and Roam carry no `roles` of their own, so once their schema reference is empty, `is_relation` becomes false and the row matches the usual node filter, `is_schema = false` and `is_relation = false`. <roam uid="9mTAGdEPX"/>
      - An instance can also be saved with an empty schema reference, when its schema is missing or refused at that moment. ENG-2324 repairs that case for types that still exist. <roam uid="Nb1ausuiY"/>
    - Who is affected? What are they trying to do, and what is stopping them? <roam uid="-bDXE42Be"/>
      - Users who import nodes from another space. The shared-node queries in `packages/database/src/lib/sharedNodes.ts` select concepts with `is_relation = false`, so a published relation with no schema is returned among the nodes. Whether it survives the later join with node content has not been checked. <roam uid="P7NYIvDHP"/>
      - Users who import relations. Queries that select `is_relation = true`, such as Roam's `discoverSharedRelations`, no longer see it, so it is not offered for import. <roam uid="xL_Fxq7Nv"/>
      - The syncing app itself. Obsidian's `ensurePublishedRelationsAccuracy` selects relations by `is_relation = true`, so it stops checking these rows. <roam uid="3qLeIwU5j"/>
      - Code that counts or lists nodes, such as the "nodes" scope of the query builder in `packages/database/src/lib/queries.ts`. <roam uid="jv5brbET0"/>
    - What request, observation, or other evidence supports this? <roam uid="q1I8ke3-2"/>
      - Found while reviewing ENG-2324, which makes the Obsidian full sync delete schemas that the plugin settings no longer have. Each such deletion empties the schema reference of every instance of that type. ENG-2324 leaves instances of a deleted type out of scope. <roam uid="nrn0zhXsl"/>
      - Code reading only: the trigger and the foreign key in `packages/database/supabase/schemas/concept.sql`, the instance writers in both apps' `conceptConversion.ts`, and the query filters listed above. Nothing has been reproduced. <roam uid="68b_bhVE-"/>
      - Roam already deletes the instances of a node schema whose page is gone (`deleteNodeSchemasFromSupabase`), so the problem mostly concerns Obsidian and relation instances. <roam uid="4eMGUDfOm"/>
  - Fit and urgency <roam uid="PYt5slXdA"/>
    - ^^What accepted user, developer, or project need would this address?^^ <roam uid="Y7cZwad_1"/>
      - Sharing nodes and relations between spaces and between apps. Importers rely on the schema reference to know an instance's type, and on `is_relation` to tell nodes from relations. <roam uid="ONQBr-2Ei"/>
    - Is it relevant to work expected within the next six months? <roam uid="pQa-rzUIt"/>
      - Yes. Cross-app import of nodes and relations is being extended now. <roam uid="IbmDRK7jq"/>
    - Why consider it now? What happens if we delay it? <roam uid="ZEzHX5IUF"/>
      - ENG-2324 makes schema deletion a normal part of the Obsidian full sync, so every deleted type now reliably leaves such instances behind. <roam uid="VXSKNHCE3"/>
      - Delay costs little while few types get deleted. The rows accumulate until something removes them. <roam uid="OQYXEFBFd"/>
  - Proposed solution <roam uid="A0K_JtfRu"/>
    - Delete the Concept row of an instance when its schema is deleted, by changing the `schema_id` foreign key to `ON DELETE CASCADE`. This applies to nodes and relations alike. <roam uid="K79QhnoSC"/>
    - Keep the instances' Content rows, so repopulating is cheap. Obsidian's full sync already sends a node again when its Concept row is missing. Relations are not re-sent that way, and Roam's behavior has not been checked. <roam uid="d_ydTfelb"/>
    - Make the sync skip instances whose type is not in the local settings. Obsidian's sync treats every note with a `nodeTypeId` as a node, whether or not that type is known, and sends a node again when its Concept row is missing. Without this, the next full sync puts each deleted row back with no schema. ENG-2324's repair already applies this filter. <roam uid="qARWlJHuQ"/>
    - Consequences to accept: spaces that imported those instances no longer see them. Their `ResourceAccess` rows remain on purpose: `on_delete_local_reference` removes them only when no Concept, Content or Document row with that `source_local_id` is left, and the kept Content rows still need them. In Obsidian, restoring the type in the settings brings its nodes back on the next full sync, but not its relations. <roam uid="Rh-ottKk3"/>
  - Alternatives considered <roam uid="mUPCiV2WH"/>
    - Keep schema-less instances usable, by writing `roles` into each relation instance or by deriving `is_relation` from the `source` and `destination` shape of its references. Rejected: it preserves data whose type no longer exists, and every query then has to cope with instances that have no schema. <roam uid="PtmBVdOqm"/>
    - Delete the instances from the client, as Roam's cleanup does. It needs the same logic in each app, where the foreign key does it once. <roam uid="USUA_ga7O"/>
    - Later, a way to block the deletion of a schema that still has instances, or to move instances in bulk to another type. Either would make the cascade rarer, not unnecessary. <roam uid="srql-Wxjn"/>
  - Triage <roam uid="sCU61yZBH"/>
    - Is the need clear enough to create an engineering ticket? <roam uid="sanS3urti"/>
    - Outcome: Ready for engineering ticket / Explore / Park / Reject <roam uid="3OTUfv269"/>
    - Reason: <roam uid="yUoOZwthO"/>
- ENG-1870: which Roam asset URLs we publish <roam uid="qxLrH9j3U" heading="1"/>
  - `isRoamStorageUrl` (`apps/roam/src/utils/findAssetReferences.ts`) currently sorts every URL in a node's markdown into two piles: an asset in Roam's known bucket, whichever graph uploaded it, which we copy into shared storage, and everything else, which we leave alone. <roam uid="2Vh-spIb2"/>
  - We propose three piles instead: <roam uid="A49XNmcfX"/>
  - {{[[table]]}} <roam uid="6Xjmc0Hn6"/>
    - URL <roam uid="ZkREnoTd5"/>
      - What we do <roam uid="Qcy5IWUgU"/>
    - Known bucket, path names this graph <roam uid="1IB7io6II"/>
      - Copy it, as today <roam uid="R9WdJjnfU"/>
    - Known bucket, path names another graph <roam uid="2JKNVbNBH"/>
      - Leave it, as an ordinary link <roam uid="CvSifxzhr"/>
    - Unknown bucket, Roam path structure <roam uid="rCZRGM3s_"/>
      - Leave it, and report the bucket to PostHog <roam uid="N6JxFOvE3"/>
    - Anything else <roam uid="3CB5kzNDh"/>
      - Leave it, as today <roam uid="div68iVKr"/>
  - Both new cases keep their original URL in the markdown, which is the existing degradation path. The two sections below make the case for each. <roam uid="p5k1unBrb"/>
  - Only this graph's assets <roam uid="P0nmLricE" heading="2"/>
    - Match the path segment against `window.roamAlphaAPI.graph.name`. Another graph's asset is left as its original URL, which keeps rendering: the Firebase token is world-readable, and destinations rewrite links only for assets that have a `FileReference`. <roam uid="OGOaBf6NA"/>
    - Copying blocks between graphs carries the source graph's asset URLs along, so this is real: 2.3% of distinct assets in the akamatsulab export are from other graphs, 7.3% in discourse-graphs. <roam uid="Qeh3yvqL7"/>
      - **For:** we copy only bytes the publisher's own graph uploaded. A Firebase download token makes another graph's asset readable, but that is not consent to redistribute it through our storage. It also bounds our storage cost and closes a cross-tenant question we would otherwise carry. <roam uid="fNOcZnAcM"/>
      - **For:** the same predicate does double duty. `imgs/app/<current graph>/` is what makes an asset ours to copy, and it is what makes an unknown bucket a credible migration signal rather than noise, so one rule covers what we store and what we alert on.\n <roam uid="iDqGbfdZn"/>
      - **Against:** those assets stay hotlinked rather than copied, so they lose durability (a deleted asset, a rotated token, or a bucket migration rots the link) and offline availability in Obsidian. Nothing stops rendering today. <roam uid="48a1XCT94"/>
  - A new bucket with the same path structure <roam uid="jNDe8Gf-a" heading="2"/>
    - The case to think about: Roam moves uploads to a new bucket, keeping `imgs/app/<graph>/`. We would match the path, recognize the graph, and be looking at what is genuinely one of our own user's assets, sitting somewhere we have never seen. <roam uid="SuyquM5zn"/>
    - We propose to **match this case but not store it**. Matching is what makes it visible: today such a URL is indistinguishable from an ordinary external link, so a Roam migration would silently stop asset publishing across every graph and we would hear about it from user reports. Matching it gives us a `posthog.capture` on the one signal that says our assumption has expired, carrying the bucket name and whether the path names the current graph, and no URL or token. That is our only detector for a change we cannot otherwise see. <roam uid="bNuKHjk6m"/>
    - Storing it is the part we would advise against. Trusting the path alone would let the extension survive a Roam bucket migration with no release, which is genuinely worth something. But it also means anyone who can get a URL into a node's markdown can point us at a Firebase bucket they own, under a path they have spelled `imgs/app/<victim graph>/`, and put bytes of their choosing into ours. The path is not evidence of ownership, only of shape. Availability through a migration is not worth an open write path, and a migration is something we can ship a release for once the warning tells us it happened. <roam uid="q6_OHNg94"/>
  - NOTE: We decided against this, but the security scenario is real: see ((d4KkPP4Tq))<ref>Security issue: Inserting a hostile file in Supabase</ref> <roam uid="3iHAJdgeN"/>
- Resolve Repeat Asset references #iss-candidate <roam uid="V0lkfGnyG" heading="1" refs="1"/>
  - Related to ((7QuBg7x0r))<ref>Which path should we save when an Obsidian note publishes an image? (resolved)</ref> <roam uid="JwElvWojR"/>
  - Why <roam uid="XJmtWO1vj" heading="2"/>
    - **Post-v0.** This change removes redundant work. It does not fix a defect, so it should be scheduled after the `cross-app-asset-references` change ships rather than folded into it. <roam uid="a0WeykGFC"/>
    - Background, for a reader arriving cold. When a Roam node is published, its markdown can embed images and files that live in Roam's storage, each written into the markdown as a URL. Publishing copies those bytes into our Supabase bucket and records one `FileReference` row per node per URL. In that row, `filepath` holds the asset URL exactly as the markdown wrote it, `filehash` holds the SHA-256 of the bytes, and `source_path` holds the name Roam stored the asset under. A destination that later imports the node finds the asset by matching the URL in the markdown against `filepath`. <roam uid="pAPEp_-7-"/>
    - Publishing copies an asset only when the node has no reference row for that URL yet. Two nodes that embed the same asset URL each need their own row, so each one downloads the same bytes and hashes them again. Every graph that later publishes a node embedding that URL downloads them again too. The `file_exists` check stops the second upload to the bucket. It does not stop the second download or the second hash. <roam uid="LaewhzJYd"/>
    - The cause is the shape of `addFile` (`packages/database/src/lib/files.ts`), not an oversight in the publish stage. `addFile` takes the bytes because it computes the hash. A caller that wants only to record a reference row has no way to ask for one without supplying content it has already accounted for. <roam uid="Tn5wj1IDs"/>
    - The waste is small. It happens on first publish only, it is bounded by `MAX_PUBLISHED_ASSET_BYTES`, and shared asset URLs are uncommon in Roam, because each upload gets its own URL and reusing one across two nodes takes a deliberate copy and paste. The reason to write this down now is that the obvious fix is the wrong one. See the last bullet below. <roam uid="_adOV8J4o"/>
  - What Changes <roam uid="_w-B5_JqO" heading="2"/>
    - **Resolve a repeat asset URL from the reference row that already describes it.** The publish stage reads the reference rows of every publishing node in one query (`readExistingReferences` in `apps/roam/src/utils/publishNodeAssets.ts`). Widen that query to also match rows by `filepath` across the space, not only by `source_local_id` for the nodes being published. Any row in the space that holds the same asset URL already carries the `filehash`, `source_path`, `created` and `last_modified` values the new row needs. This is sound because a Roam storage URL names one immutable upload: re-uploading a file produces a new URL, so the same URL always names the same bytes. <roam uid="Lm2fcTtsL"/>
    - **Add a function beside `addFile` that inserts a reference row against a known hash.** It is the second half of `addFile`, the `FileReference` insert and its duplicate-key update, without the hashing, the `file_exists` check, and the bucket upload. Without it there is no way to record a reference row except by supplying bytes, so the previous bullet is not usable on its own. <roam uid="lmYvSs9xC"/>
    - **A repeat asset URL then costs no download and no hash.** It resolves through a query the publish stage already runs, and holds no bytes in memory. <roam uid="pPXOAsvK9"/>
    - **Do not add a byte cache.** Two versions were considered and both are rejected. A cache scoped to one publish run helps only duplicates that fall in the same batch. A cache that counts references first and evicts as it goes needs a lifetime, an eviction rule, and a memory ceiling, and the ceiling is still unbounded when many distinct assets are duplicated at once. Both exist only to satisfy `addFile`'s demand for bytes. Removing that demand is smaller and it works across separate publish runs, so a node published next week gets the same saving. <roam uid="gZYZhuhS8"/>
    - No **BREAKING** changes. The result is invisible from outside: the same rows, against the same stored bytes, holding the same values. <roam uid="HmjofFQkA"/>

Nothing in the CI output says this, so a failure can name a file that does not exist on the branch, and the developer cannot tell whether their own code is broken or the stack has fallen behind `main`. <roam uid="HoKtpbu3H"/>

      - The error names a file that `git log` and `git show` prove is absent from the branch, which reads as CI testing the wrong thing. <roam uid="PKWvgEfY2"/>
      - `pnpm ci:validate` passes locally on the exact commit CI rejected, because the local checkout has no `main` content in it. <roam uid="w1D4nQgpV"/>

    - Observed on September 17, on pull request #1462 (`eng-2280`). Following the parents of `3b92633ed` gives `merge(eng-2219, merge(eng-2247, merge(eng-2217, 3eee92b49)))`, and `3eee92b49` is `main`. The file came in from `main`. <roam uid="TLpmPqyQp"/>

    - ^^What accepted user, developer, or project need would this address?^^ <roam uid="TM64PXOit"/>
      - Developers need a CI failure to identify what was tested, so they can separate a defect in their own branch from a conflict with `main`. The team adopted `gh stack` for the cross-app asset work, and stacked pull requests are now a normal way to ship here. <roam uid="Wqrr-819-"/>

      - The fix is small and sits in one file, `.github/workflows/ci.yaml`. Three changes, in order of value: <roam uid="eSK51Bkjh"/>
        - Add `edited` to the `pull_request` trigger types so that correcting a base re-runs CI. Pair it with a `concurrency` group and `cancel-in-progress`, because `edited` also fires on title and body edits. <roam uid="2f_jpCaZC"/>

- Stop the asset copy from destroying an iframe embed of a Roam-hosted file #iss-candidate <roam uid="yA8YwTUc5" heading="1" refs="1"/>
  - My assessment: A real bug, almost certainly rare. Probably post-v0. <roam uid="FhnRTz0xr" refs="1"/>
  - Need / Problem Statement <roam uid="4DUmX3q-G" heading="2"/>
    - What is the problem that you are trying to solve? <roam uid="f_xDzsGcF"/>
      - The problem is: when a published node embeds one of its own uploaded files in an `{{iframe: url}}` block, the import records that file as an asset and then rewrites the block's URL in a form the iframe cannot use, so the embed arrives broken. <roam uid="HchJinGmq"/>
    - Background, for a reader who has not worked on the asset copy <roam uid="VvHrNBT7v"/>
      - Publishing a node copies the files it references into shared storage, so a reader in another graph can open them. The publisher scans the node's markdown for URLs, keeps the ones that point at this graph's own Roam uploads, and writes one `FileReference` row per file. The row's `filepath` column holds the URL exactly as the markdown wrote it. <roam uid="snBL-tFTk"/>
      - Importing the node reverses this. The importer scans the same markdown, looks up each URL it finds against those rows, and replaces the ones that match with the URL of the copy in the reader's own graph. <roam uid="gcDMS2Wv6"/>
      - Both scans read a list of link shapes, and the list ends with a bare URL case that claims any URL the earlier shapes left. The two lists are not identical, but neither one has a case for an iframe, so an iframe's URL reaches the bare URL case on both sides. <roam uid="Q0ys3GU9b"/>
    - Who is affected? What are they trying to do, and what is stopping them? <roam uid="yevHirw1P"/>
      - A Roam author who embedded their own uploaded file in an iframe rather than in one of the media embeds Roam writes by itself. They are trying to publish that node and have a reader in another graph see the same page. The embed does not survive the round trip. <roam uid="tv961e2iz"/>
      - Roam never writes this shape on its own. `file.upload` produces an image, pdf, audio or video embed, or a plain link. So reaching this needs an author who typed the iframe deliberately, which makes it uncommon rather than impossible. <roam uid="K1P17qfl4"/>
    - What request, observation, or other evidence supports this? <roam uid="zZV_dVUGx"/>
      - Found while reviewing the fix for ENG-2289, then reproduced by running the publisher's scan straight into the importer's rewrite. <roam uid="Qde0DmwA1"/>
      - The node's markdown holds one iframe embed of a file uploaded to this graph. <roam uid="0dYSp1EAc"/>
        - `{{iframe: https://firebasestorage.../o/imgs%2Fapp%2FMAPLab%2Fpaper.pdf?alt=media&token=abc}}` <roam uid="b1b-5P38A"/>
      - Publishing records one row for it, under the URL exactly as the markdown wrote it. The URL reached the bare URL case, and the filter that follows kept it, because it does point at this graph's uploads. <roam uid="gsAHHCYIC"/>
        - `["https://firebasestorage.../o/imgs%2Fapp%2FMAPLab%2Fpaper.pdf?alt=media&token=abc"]` <roam uid="O0FMwPaG_"/>
      - Importing finds that row from the same bare URL case, reads the file's type as pdf, and writes a pdf embed in place of the URL. The pdf embed lands inside the iframe braces the author wrote, and the iframe is destroyed. <roam uid="94-lILYN_"/>
        - `{{iframe: {{[[pdf]]: https://reader.example/storage/paper.pdf}}}}` <roam uid="HEkbD61Ox"/>
      - An external URL in an iframe produces no row and is left alone, so this reaches only files uploaded to the publishing graph. <roam uid="RrWwEw6LJ"/>
      - What remains unverified is how Roam renders that nested result. The strings above are what our code produces, checked directly. <roam uid="WDiLhtSDR"/>

This is the same need ENG-2289 addressed for the media embeds, reached by a different route: ENG-2289 fixed damage done by Roam's markdown parser, and this is damage done by our own rewrite. <roam uid="2T0Kp6o8u"/>

    - Is the need clear enough to create an engineering ticket? <roam uid="9YS4osiRa"/>
      - The behavior is confirmed. What is undecided is the intended result, and that is a product question: either leave an iframe's URL alone and copy no file for it, or copy the file and write the new URL back inside the iframe braces. <roam uid="knZm4-etm"/>
      - Leaving it alone is the cheaper of the two. The reader's graph would keep pointing at the publishing graph's storage URL, which is already the documented assumption for an asset whose copy failed: the original may still render for the reader. <roam uid="0wt1DMT4I"/>
      - Sequencing, once the result is decided <roam uid="1xN1rJl5A"/>
        - Fix the importer first. It is the necessary side and is safe to ship alone, because rows for these assets already exist and only the importer can stop them from nesting on every past publish. <roam uid="UT-58ZNuN"/>
        - The publisher is optional and can follow. Fixing it alone fixes nothing, since the existing rows remain. Leaving it unfixed costs one row and one copied file that nobody reads. <roam uid="ogS926biq"/>
        - The two sides do not have to move together. Every case in both scans captures the URL through the same group, so which case claims a URL never changes the string that is recorded or looked up. <roam uid="stKCGZt5H"/>
        - Inside the importer, one thing does have to move together: it reads its matches by position, so adding a case shifts every later position and the code that reads them has to shift with it. The publisher reads its matches by value and is not affected. <roam uid="5ei5pkpD7"/>
      - Outcome: Explore <roam uid="Rx58vpzgW"/>
      - Reason: The mechanism is confirmed and the fix is small, but the intended result is a product decision rather than a bug with one obvious answer. <roam uid="xGDV9tHVX"/>

    - What is the problem that you are trying to solve? <roam uid="Y6IyHNnyJ"/>
      - The problem is: when a node published from Roam is imported into Obsidian, an attachment that is not an image, PDF, audio or video is downloaded into the vault, but the note keeps pointing at Roam's storage server instead of at the downloaded copy. <roam uid="sBwLoZ-0s"/>
        - Background for anyone arriving cold: a user can publish a discourse node from one app and import it into the other. Assets travel with the node. The importer downloads each asset into the destination vault or graph, then rewrites the links in the note so they point at the local copy rather than at the origin app's storage. <roam uid="nneuYcgrM"/>
    - Who is affected? What are they trying to do, and what is stopping them? <roam uid="bxv5e7u_7"/>
      - An Obsidian user importing a shared node that was published from Roam, where the node has a `.docx`, `.csv`, `.zip` or any other attachment Roam does not treat as media. <roam uid="_cREg0f4e"/>
      - They want to open the attachment from the imported note. The link they get instead leaves Obsidian, needs network access and a live Roam access token, and stops working when the token expires or when the origin graph is no longer reachable. <roam uid="-61pnRFyM"/>
      - The file they need is already in the vault. Nothing points at it, so it reads as a stray download. <roam uid="H9U1fOC4-"/>
      - The link text is the raw storage URL, roughly 200 characters of host, escaped path and token, rather than the file's name. A reader cannot tell what the attachment is without opening it. <roam uid="e2ARfwTRl"/>
    - What request, observation, or other evidence supports this? <roam uid="dtNKuwPvb"/>
      - Found by reading the code while scoping the remaining test scenarios for ENG-1873. Not yet reproduced in a vault. Every claim below was verified in the source; the re-import claim under Fit and urgency is the one exception and is marked. <roam uid="mlGmorO_K"/>
      - Roam's `file.upload` returns a bare URL for anything it does not recognise as an image, PDF, audio or video. The published markdown then carries that URL on its own, with no surrounding markdown link. Example shape: `https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/firescript-577a2.appspot.com/o/imgs%2Fapp%2F{graph}%2F{uid}.docx?alt=media&token={token}` <roam uid="J_eluuAr7"/>
      - `importAssetsForNode` in `apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts` iterates the rows in `file_references`, not the links in the markdown. So the attachment is downloaded and written into the vault under its recorded name whatever shape the link has. <roam uid="8q_hNdCcU"/>
      - `updateMarkdownAssetLinks`, in the same file, rewrites exactly three shapes: `[[wikilink]]`, `[text](path)` and `![alt](path)`. A bare URL matches none of the three regexes, so it is never touched. The two halves disagree: the download half is driven by database rows, the rewrite half by link shape. <roam uid="C8GVGrfM-"/>
      - The Roam importer already handles this case, so the design is settled and only one direction is missing it. `rewriteAssetLinks.ts` in `apps/roam` carries a reference form named `bare` alongside `embed` and `link`, and a `labelFor` helper whose comment states that without it the label would come out as the storage URL. <roam uid="J3wOVRgP3"/>
      - Nothing covers it in tests. `apps/obsidian` had no asset tests at all until ENG-2254 added vitest, so this is now testable without new infrastructure. <roam uid="WCCEttIh1"/>
    - What would fix it <roam uid="ERGm8XiFb"/>
      - Resolve a bare URL through the same row lookup the image branch already uses for an external URL, then write `[{name}]({local path})`, taking the name from the `source_path` column, which holds the name the publishing app kept the file under. <roam uid="LfeeRePwx"/>
      - Leave a bare URL with no matching row exactly as written. Matching is by row lookup rather than by URL shape, so an ordinary hyperlink a user typed cannot be caught by accident. <roam uid="z-M4gBLL4"/>
      - One hazard worth pricing in: Obsidian runs three independent `.replace()` passes, so a fourth pass added naively would also re-match the URLs inside `[text](url)` and `![alt](url)` that the earlier passes already rewrote. Roam avoided this with a single alternation scan, and its comment says so explicitly. Matching that structure in Obsidian is the cleaner fix and the wider diff, in a function that is already long. <roam uid="iuNDjhRFg"/>
